summary: Project a real x-z wavevector from a nonnegative magnitude and angle, or compute magnitude from paired components already expressed in inverse metres.

identity.relation: Real x-z plane wavevector declaration to perpendicular and parallel components and magnitude
identity.direction: k and theta_rad -> kx, kz, k; or paired kx and kz -> kx, kz, k
identity.definition: Polar: kx = k sin(theta_rad), kz = k cos(theta_rad). Cartesian: k = hypot(kx, kz). The two input modes are exclusive.
identity.model: Euclidean wavevector geometry, without a dispersion or resonance model
identity.geometry: Background field along z; real wavevector in the x-z plane
identity.coordinates: Cartesian x-z components with z parallel to the background field
identity.boundary: Magnitude is nonnegative; zero magnitude keeps the supplied polar angle, whereas Cartesian mode returns no angle.
assumptions: The caller has converted all wave numbers to consistent inverse-metre units.
The operation does not rotate coordinates or handle a y component.

inputs.name: k_grid
inputs.description: Wavevector magnitude sweep in polar mode.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty, one-dimensional, finite and nonnegative; boolean pseudo-numbers are rejected even where NumPy would coerce a mixed container such as [1, True] to integers; exclusive with component grids.

inputs.name: theta_rad
inputs.description: Propagation angle from +z toward +x; ignored in Cartesian mode.
inputs.constraints: Defaults to zero in polar mode and must be finite there; boolean and string surrogates are rejected.

inputs.name: kx_grid
inputs.description: Perpendicular component sweep in Cartesian mode.
inputs.constraints: Requires a same-length kz_grid; boolean pseudo-numbers are rejected; exclusive with k_grid.

inputs.name: kz_grid
inputs.description: Parallel component sweep in Cartesian mode.
inputs.constraints: Requires a same-length kx_grid; boolean pseudo-numbers are rejected; exclusive with k_grid.

outputs.name: theta_rad
outputs.description: Declared polar angle or null in Cartesian mode.

preconditions: Caller has already converted all wave numbers to 1/m.
Arrays are finite real vectors; paired components have equal length.
supported: Single-angle polar sweeps and paired Cartesian component sweeps in the x-z plane.
excluded: Scan-driver selection, logarithmic controls, parameter-state updates and derived angle output.
Complex wavevectors, y components, coordinate rotations and dispersion physics.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for missing or mixed modes, non-real or nonfinite vectors, boolean pseudo-numbers including mixed containers that NumPy would coerce (for example [1, True]), negative polar magnitude, non-real or nonfinite polar angle, invalid component shape, or nonfinite computed Cartesian magnitude.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Unexpected NumPy execution errors propagate; malformed numeric input is rejected as invalid input.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; there is no iteration.
failure_semantics.partial_results: None; the result dictionary is returned only after validation and calculation complete.

example.description: Compute the magnitude of a caller-supplied 3-4 Cartesian wavevector in inverse metres.
example.code:
from scirel.geometry import project_planar_wavevector
result = project_planar_wavevector(kx_grid=[3.0], kz_grid=[4.0])
assert result['k'][0] == 5.0
example.expected: The result keeps kx=[3], kz=[4] and computes k=[5] with theta_rad unset.

scope: Non-real input rejection including string and boolean pseudo-numbers in pure and mixed containers, nonfinite magnitude rejection and large finite hypot behavior.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The direct tests establish this callable's declared bounded arithmetic, boolean-pseudo-number rejection and failure behaviour in this tree. No external cross-implementation comparison is re-runnable from this repository, and none is claimed as evidence here.
known_limitations: Wave numbers supplied in normalized input-card units lack a verified conversion to 1/m.
The mapping is exercised only on real numeric inputs; string and boolean numeric surrogates are rejected by SciRel and lie outside every existing comparison.
The Cartesian norm deliberately avoids the squared-sum overflow that a naive square-and-sum evaluation shows at large finite components.
Scan-driver state semantics require a separate relation.
